## 2. Exact result accepted

For every fixed integer m>=2, W=m^2, original S>=0,a>0, and the specified COMMON numerator P1, I accept:

    total_degree(P1)=W-1,
    H_m(S,a) >= B_m(S+a)^(W-1),
    B_m=m^(2W+2)(W-1)(m+2)/2>0,

where H_m is its top homogeneous component and the bound extends to the nonnegative axes with S+a>0. I accept the exact formula through the explicitly defined limiting R_lambda. Both pure-axis coefficients are positive; positivity of every mixed coefficient is not inferred.

For the finite rational absolute coefficient sum A_m of P1-H_m, the sufficient rational threshold R_m=1+2A_m/B_m gives

    S+a>=R_m => P1(S,a)>=(B_m/2)(S+a)^(W-1)>0.

This is a valid coefficient-defined uniform pointwise sum tail for P1 only. Neither A_m nor R_m has been evaluated, and there is no numerical interval coverage, practical complexity claim, or proof for the full trace at arbitrary c. The merged scalar m>=3 small-x limitation and Jensen bound are also correct. The remaining mixed/lower coefficient signs, moderate/small-s P1 sign, trace/HCM0 and mother Goal remain OPEN.

## 3. Removing U(r0) is legitimate only before changing parameters

The derivatives of the original rising-factorial columns form a basis of polynomials of degree at most m-2 in theta. Their coefficient matrix U(r0) is triangular with nonzero rational leading entries and is independent of L. The derivative-average formula therefore gives G_L=Y F_L(J)U(r0) exactly, where J is differentiation on this n-dimensional polynomial space and J^n=0. This is the n-by-n coefficient differentiator, not an unexplained reuse of an ambient m-by-m inverse.

For the derivative defining K, r0 is fixed. Hence H=U^T Hbar U really makes K similar to Kbar without a missing U' term. Direct multiplication of Hbar=F^T Q_r F gives

    F Kbar F^-1 = Gamma_L + Q_r^-1 Gamma_L^T Q_r + Q_r^-1 Q_r'.

Both frame terms remain. Derivation of this identity precedes substitution of lambda=L/r. It is not differentiation along a path with fixed lambda. No claim that an r0-dependent congruence is constant while r0 varies is needed: the exact identity holds at every physical point, and is only then used to compare those points asymptotically.

## 4. The metric germ has the stated powers and is uniform in the ratio

For monomial indices 0<=j,k<=m-2, the factor outside the alternating metric sum is r^(j+k-m). Finite differences at spacing 1/m kill every theta_i^q with q<n and give (-1)^n n!/m^n at q=n. In the two-variable analytic germ, a term u^q t^b contributes t^(q+b); all q<n terms vanish, including b>0 terms. At order n only q=n,b=0 remains. Thus

    Q_r[j,k]=r^(j+k-2m+1)(M[j,k]+O(1/r)),
    M[j,k]=kappa binom(-m,m-1-j-k).

The exponent agrees with alpha_j+alpha_k for alpha_j=j-m+1/2. Factoring the exact finite-difference zero leaves a function analytic in t=1/r. This proves the differentiated estimate r A_r'=O(1/r); it does not differentiate an unsupported asymptotic symbol. Q_r, C_r and A_r depend only on the terminal r, not on r0 and L separately. This is the actual reason the remainder can be uniform in lambda.

## 5. I checked the centered residue/Fourier Gram argument independently

The coefficient form is kappa times Res_0 f(u)g(u)du/[u^m(1+u)^m]. Under z=u/(1+u), the weight becomes z^-m(1-z)^(2m-2)dz and the centered coordinate u+1/2 becomes (1+z)/(2(1-z)). The resulting powers are Laurent polynomials; in particular j+k<=2m-4 prevents a pole on the integration circle.

With z=exp(i theta), (1-z) contributes -2i exp(i theta/2)sin(theta/2), and (1+z)/(1-z)=i cot(theta/2). The phase from dz cancels the remaining exponential. The sign (-1)^(m-1) of kappa cancels the same sign from (-2i)^(2m-2), leaving precisely the factor |kappa|2^(2m-2)i^(j+k)/2^(j+k) in formula(7).

Odd j+k integrates to zero by theta -> 2pi-theta. Within one parity, i^(j+k)=(-1)^p epsilon_j epsilon_k. The weight is positive in the interior and has enough endpoint vanishing: 2m-2-j-k>=2. Distinct monomials in cot(theta/2) are linearly independent on (0,2pi). This proves a strictly positive Gram form before the stated sign and epsilon congruence. The centered even-degree block is positive definite and the odd-degree block negative definite. The possibly empty block at m=2 is harmless. Thus M is nonsingular; no generic definite-metric or finite-r real-spectrum assumption is made.

## 6. Gamma reflection and centered parity are exact, not asymptotic guesses

In the truncated commutative polynomial ring in J, F_-L=exp(-LJ)F_L is exact. Differentiating with respect to L includes the minus sign from the argument -L and yields Gamma_-L=J-Gamma_L. Homogeneity gives a finite sum b_k L^(k-1)J^k, so the reflection identity forces b_1=1/2 and all odd k>=3 coefficients to vanish. Only J/2 and even positive powers of J remain; no Bernoulli coefficient sign is assumed.

Since C_r J C_r^-1=J/r, multiplication by r gives exactly gamma_lambda(J), including a regular lambda=0 endpoint. The scaling of the adjoint term and Q_r' term gives the exact displayed transformed matrix

    Z_lambda + A_r^-1 Z_lambda^T A_r + r A_r^-1 A_r'.

There is no omitted transpose or second diagonal derivative. Here Z_lambda=D_alpha+gamma_lambda. In the centered variable v=u+1/2, D_alpha+J/2 is v*d/dv-(m-1/2)I; all remaining derivatives have even order. Thus Z_lambda preserves centered parity for every lambda, not just at 0 or 1. M has the same orthogonal blocks, so R_lambda=Z_lambda+M^-1 Z_lambda^T M preserves them and satisfies R_lambda^T M=M R_lambda.

Changing the sign of the negative block gives positive definite block metrics and makes R_lambda similar blockwise to real symmetric matrices. Hence the real-eigenvalue bound applies for each lambda in [0,1]. The trace of gamma_lambda is zero by nilpotence, so

    tr R_lambda=2 sum_(j=0)^(m-2)(j-m+1/2)=-(W-1).

The resulting square bound is tr(R_lambda^2)>=(W-1)^2/(m-1). After adding W-1 it is exactly (W-1)(m+2). This applies ONLY to R_lambda, never to the original indefinite finite-r K or Omega.

## 7. The error estimate survives both potentially large similarities

For large r, A_r and A_r^-1 lie in a fixed analytic neighborhood of M; their error and the derivative error depend only on r. gamma_lambda is a finite polynomial on the compact interval [0,1]. The explicit transformed matrix therefore differs from R_lambda by O_m(1/r) uniformly in lambda. Squared trace has the same uniform estimate because all these transformed matrices are uniformly bounded.

This argument never estimates the norm of F, U(r0) or C_r: trace similarity is an exact identity at each physical point. Their possible large condition numbers do not enter the remainder. This also handles ratios tending to zero, even when the physical first gap is arbitrarily small. The original secant is polynomial at L=0 and F_L has no 1/L pole. The lambda=0 endpoint is a limit for the proof and a polynomial boundary, not an assertion that the physical first gap equals zero.

## 8. All scale factors, total degree and the exact top form

The original fixed-denominator formula is

    P1=(W/2)(x+beta)G_W(x)[tr(K^2)+W q_W(x)], x=mr.

The finite scalar sums give x^2 q_W=W-1+O_m(1/x). Therefore r^2 Wq_W=W-1+O_m(1/r), because W=m^2. The monic G_W contributes x^W, and (W/2)(x+beta) contributes W x/2 at leading order. Hence the leading multiplier in r is m^(W+3)/2. Substituting r=m(S+a) contributes the further m^(W-1), producing exactly m^(2W+2)/2 in(13)-(14). No m from either the derivative, x, or r-to-s substitution is lost.

For every positive direction, the finite limit of P1(tS,ta)/t^(W-1) forces all higher homogeneous components to vanish on the positive quadrant. They are polynomials, hence identically zero. The strictly positive limit makes the total degree exactly W-1. This argument is joint-degree reasoning; it is stronger than the old fixed-S a-degree limit and is not imported from that limit.

The exact H_m formula extends to lambda=0 and 1. Its polynomial nature follows from being the top component; independently gamma_lambda has degree at most n-2 for n>=2, and the squared trace degree at most 2n-4<=W-1, with n<=2 constant cases. Multiplication by (S+a)^(W-1) clears those ratio powers. Continuity and the uniform spectral bound give H_m>=B_m(S+a)^(W-1) on both nonnegative axes. This proves the two pure-axis coefficients positive. It gives no sign theorem for each mixed monomial coefficient, and the manuscript correctly keeps that distinction.

## 9. The coefficient-defined uniform threshold is mathematically sufficient

For fixed m, P1 is an already specified finite rational polynomial, and H_m is its top part. Thus A_m is a well-defined nonnegative rational number, obtainable by finite exact algebra in principle. Its value, a coefficient table and an execution cost have not been supplied.

The remainder has degree at most W-2. On S,a>=0, s=S+a>=1, each remainder monomial has magnitude at most s^(W-2). The triangle inequality consequently gives |P1-H_m|<=A_m s^(W-2). For s>=1+2A_m/B_m, this is at most (B_m/2)s^(W-1). The claimed positive lower bound follows, including the A_m=0 case. No compact coverage or practical numerical threshold is hidden in this existence-by-finite-coefficients result.

In particular the theorem is about P1 on a large-s region. It is not a sign theorem for the full original trace T(c) when c is arbitrary. It does not establish that the permanently stopped m7 compact interval r in[7,8] meets the condition: an unevaluated R_m supplies no such comparison and no runtime authorization.

## 10. Retained scalar result, bounded dedup and final limits

I rechecked the carried scalar section. Jensen gives h2>=(W-1)/(x+beta)^2>0. The formula q_W(0)=4H_W/(W+1)-H_W^(2)-4/(W+1)^2 and decreasing H_N/(N+1) give the stated negative bound for W>=9, namely at most -241/1050-4/(W+1)^2. Taking S=0,a=x/W>0 makes the continuity interval physical. The large-x limit is positive. This still gives no small-x curvature compensation and no negative P1 example. F736's genuine scalar contribution is retained in the one combined unit rather than counted as an independent vote.

The old all-m positive tangent is the different P0 face; the old whole-trace carrier specifies all coefficients implicitly but leaves its signed domination open. The inspected finite m3..6 results are stronger for those particular m and are not counted anew. The new V2 gain is the dimension-free pointwise-positive top homogeneous P1 face and the uniform coefficient-defined sum tail. Bounded dedup remains limited to the actual inputs identified above; no repository-wide or historical novelty claim is accepted.

I find no mathematical mustfix for the complete enhanced proof with these limits. My V1 report and context remain unchanged historical artifacts; this new report supplies the separate complete V2 assessment, within the same bounded unit.
